newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sailor shatters round-the-world record.
newsitem.headline: French sailor shatters round-the-world record.

text.p: French sailor Olivier de Kersauson set a new round-the-world sailing record on Monday, shaving nearly three days off the old record by circling the globe in 71 days, 14 hours, 18 minutes and eight seconds.
The previous record of 74 days 22 hours and 17 minutes had been set by New Zealander Sir Peter Blake in 1994.
De Kersauson and his crew of six aboard his trimaran Sport-Elec crossed the finish line at 0659 GMT, assuring him the Jules Verne trophy offered for sailing around the world in under 80 days.
"We aren't the best of sailors, we didn't have the best of boats, but we have the cheekiest crew in the world," de Kersauson said after reaching the western French port of Brest.
"We went in search of the trophy where no one else has ever gone, and we are truly happy," he told a reporter.

Named after author Jules Verne's 1872 novel Around the World in 80 Days, the race ends at an imaginary line across the Channel between the southernmost tip of Britain's Lizard Point and France's Ouessant Island.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe, in the midst of a closely contested parliamentary election campaign, quickly issued a congratulatory message to de Kersauson expressing his admiration.
"We are all proud of what you have accomplished," Juppe said.

President Jacques Chirac, in a separate message, said the "extraordinary victory...confirms the very great talent of our sailors and brings to France a pride and elan that can only be achieved in the winning of a great challenge".
The conservative Chirac has urged a "new elan" and a "shared elan" for France in his campaign messages urging a victory for the governing centre-right.
Tens of thousands of fans were waiting to greet de Kersauson and his crew when they arrived in Brest, which they left on March 8.

"When you realise the difficulty of going around the world in under 80 days, to succeed in 71 is extraordinary," said Blake, the former record-holder from New Zealand, as he presented the trophy to de Kersauson.
"The best thing that can happen to a record is to realise that it can be beaten," Blake said, predicting that new technology would one day enable a sailing yacht to circle the globe in 65 days.

In setting the previous round-the-world record in 1994, Blake's trimaran Enza-New Zealand broke a record of 79 days six hours and 15 minutes set a year earlier by France's Bruno Peyron on his trimaran Commodore explorer.
